report.title: [Evidence guided] Persistent Datapatch bug
report.body:
### Platforms

Android

### Build

BE 27790

### Issue

When you save a datapatch in a map, suddenly, attempting to remove it does not work.
When you remove it, it gets temporarily removed, but gets added back when you open the map.
I tested this with or without mods and it still happened by the way.

### Steps to reproduce

Make map
Add data-patch
Save map
Delete data-patch
Save map
Leave editor
Come back to map editor
See that the data-patch is back.

### Mods used

I tested it in vanilla but here are the mods I usually use.

Auto Research (gone from in-game mod browser?)
Patch Editor (I think this mod doesn't cause the issue)
Patch Viewer
CLaJ

### Save file

I zipped the msav here

[persistent datapatch bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32028828/persistent.datapatch.bug.zip)

### (Crash) logs

_No response_

### REPRO recording guidance (not part of the upstream report)

A previous local attempt reached the reported sequence, but the final oracle omitted its recorded initial-save screenshot. Two of five independent replay judgments were inconclusive because that prerequisite was not visible in the selected evidence. This is a fresh attempt; those prior judgments do not establish the current result.

Capture and select the important checkpoints in chronological order: the map identity and existing patch, visible successful initial save, confirmed deletion with an empty list, visible successful save after deletion, exit/reopen of the same map, and the patch list after reopening. Include both successful-save screenshots in the final sequence oracle, within its eight-checkpoint limit. Use neutral labels for the resulting state; inspect what is actually visible rather than assuming disappearance or reappearance. If prerequisites cannot be demonstrated, report that limitation.

spec.summary: Reported persistent datapatch deletion issue: after deleting a datapatch from a saved map and reopening the map editor, the datapatch is reported to be present again.
spec.observed_behavior: The reporter states that a datapatch can appear to be removed during editing, but is present again after saving, leaving the editor, and reopening the map. The report says this was also observed when tested without mods.
spec.expected_behavior: After a datapatch is deleted and the map is saved, reopening the same map should retain the deletion.
known_preconditions: A map that can be created or edited and supports datapatches.
A datapatch has been added to the map before attempting deletion.
uncertain_conditions: The reported behavior has not been independently verified.
It is unknown whether the linked ZIP contains the relevant map save, a reproducible starting state, or valid/unmodified data.
It is unknown whether the map was saved successfully both before deletion and after deletion.
It is unknown whether the same map was reopened after leaving the editor.
It is unknown whether the datapatch list was empty immediately after deletion or whether the apparent removal affected only the current UI state.
The exact Mindustry version/commit corresponding to build BE 27790 is not established; a target commit was supplied separately but not confirmed by the report.
The report names Android, while Linux is listed as a planned evaluation platform; cross-platform applicability is unknown.
The vanilla test configuration, mod disablement procedure, and whether a restart occurred between tests are not specified.
The listed mods' versions and whether any were enabled during the reported failing run are unknown.
No crash log was provided; it is unknown whether any errors or warnings occurred during saving or reopening.
reproduction_hints: Create or open a map in the editor.
Reopen the same map and inspect its datapatches.
Record the map identity, datapatch state before and after deletion, and the outcome of each save to distinguish UI-only removal from persisted removal.
required_artifacts: The linked `persistent.datapatch.bug.zip` file, including its contents and checksum if available.
The original `.msav` map file before reproduction, or a minimal map save that reproduces the report.
The map file after the initial save and after the post-deletion save, to compare persisted state.

Screenshots or video showing: map identity; datapatch present initially; successful initial save; datapatch list immediately after deletion; successful save after deletion; exit and reopening of the same map; datapatch list after reopening.
Game version/build information from the evaluated client, including commit/revision if available.
Device model, Android version, and relevant storage/location details for the map.
Enabled-mod list with mod versions for the failing run and for the vanilla comparison.
Relevant runtime/editor logs around both save operations and map reopening, if the game provides them.

hypotheses.statement: A datapatch deleted from a saved map will reappear after saving and reopening that same map.
hypotheses.prediction: The datapatch list is empty immediately after deletion but contains the same datapatch when the map is reopened.
hypotheses.observation: A test map's single <unnamed> datapatch was visible after the initial save, removed from the UI, saved again, and was visible again after quitting and reopening the named map.

steps.semantic: Open map editor from main menu
Return to map information with datapatch added
Open menu to save map containing datapatch
Open editor menu to remove datapatch
Leave empty datapatch list after deletion
Open editor menu to leave saved map
Quit editor and return to map list
Confirm leaving editor after saving deletion
Reopen the same custom map after saved deletion
Open named map in editor for post-reopen inspection
Inspect datapatches after reopening same saved map

oracle.description: The reporter states that a datapatch can appear to be removed during editing, but is present again after saving, leaving the editor, and reopening the map. The report says this was also observed when tested without mods.

findings.root_cause: The confirmed deletion path removes the PatchAsset only from DataManager's per-type patch Seq and rebuilds the UI. It does not call DataManager.reloadPatches (or otherwise rebuild orderedAssets). Map saving serializes orderedAssets via getAllAssets(), so it can write the stale pre-deletion asset list. On reopen, readDataPatches loads that serialized patch again.
findings.subsystem: Map editor embedded data-asset editing and map-save serialization

evidence: Lines 84-89 confirm deletion removes the selected object only with `patches.remove(patch)` and then calls `diag.rebuild()`; no DataManager reload/rebuild operation follows.
Lines 31 and 130 show `patches` is `state.data.getPatches()`, the DataManager-owned per-type collection.
In contrast, lines 125-143 add/replace patches and then invoke `state.data.reloadPatches(patches)`, which is absent from deletion.
candidates.reasoning: This is the most direct source of the reported UI-versus-persisted-state split: the visual list is rebuilt from the now-empty per-type collection, but DataManager's save-facing aggregate can remain stale.

evidence: Lines 169-176 show `reloadPatches` unapplies/reapplies patches and calls `rebuildOrderedAssets()`.
Lines 244-256 rebuild `orderedAssets` by copying all per-type collections.
Lines 263-265 return `orderedAssets` directly from `getAllAssets()`, while lines 293-306 show `getPatches()` returns the mutable per-type collection.
Therefore mutating the collection returned by `getPatches()` does not itself update `orderedAssets`.
candidates.reasoning: This establishes the stale-cache mechanism connecting the missing reload in the deletion handler to persistence. It also explains why adding/replacing, which calls `reloadPatches`, would not have the same aggregate-list staleness.

evidence: Lines 595-615 write the patch/assets save region from `state.data.getAllAssets()` and serialize every asset in that aggregate.
Lines 554-589 read every serialized asset into a new Seq, fire the load event, and call `state.data.load(assets)`.
A stale PatchAsset remaining in `getAllAssets()` at lines 598-601 is consequently written and later reloaded.
candidates.reasoning: This is the persistence endpoint that makes the in-memory aggregate discrepancy observable after save, exit, and reopen. It is not itself shown to mutate incorrectly; it faithfully serializes its supplied aggregate.

evidence: Lines 120-125 remove a bundle from its per-type collection and only rebuild the dialog, mirroring the patch deletion pattern.
DataManager's ordered aggregate is rebuilt only by explicit reload/load paths (DataManager.java lines 244-256), not automatically by collection removal.
candidates.reasoning: This is corroborating evidence of a broader editor asset-removal pattern and may imply an analogous persistence risk for bundles. It is lower ranked because the reported replay deletes a datapatch, not a bundle.

limitations: Only source was inspected; no game client was run and no supplied screenshot, ZIP, map-save bytes, or runtime logs were available through the tools.

The report identifies Android/build BE 27790 while source provenance relative to the replay commit was not independently established. The control/data flow in the inspected source nevertheless directly matches the supplied deterministic replay.
This localizes a cause consistent with the report, but does not determine the future human fix or prove whether other asset types are intended to refresh their runtime loaders on deletion.

patch_rationale.explanation:
Cause: the delete confirmation at MapPatchesView.java:84-89 removes the PatchAsset from the mutable per-type sequence returned by `state.data.getPatches()` but only rebuilds the dialog. `DataManager` maintains a separate `orderedAssets` aggregate: `reloadPatches()` rebuilds it (DataManager.java:169-176), while `getAllAssets()` returns that aggregate directly (DataManager.java:263-265). Saving serializes `getAllAssets()` (SaveVersion.java:595-601), so without a reload the save can still contain the deleted patch and loading restores it.

The added line calls the same patch reload path already used after add/replace in MapPatchesView.java:125-143. It unapplies the old patch effects, applies the remaining patches, and rebuilds `orderedAssets`. Thus the save-facing aggregate no longer includes the deleted PatchAsset before the UI is rebuilt, so a subsequent map save should persist the deletion.

This is a one-line, datapatch-only change in the confirmed deletion handler; it does not alter serialization, save format, the regression oracle, or unrelated asset behavior.
risks: Deleting a patch now immediately reapplies all remaining patches. This is consistent with add/replace behavior, but reviewers should verify that removing a patch is intended to revert its runtime content effects immediately, not only update persisted editor state.

`reloadPatches` may have a perceptible cost or expose errors from remaining malformed patches at deletion time; this follows the established add/replace path and is preferable to retaining stale serialized state.
Other asset editors may have analogous stale-aggregate deletion paths, but they are deliberately out of scope for this datapatch replay and are not changed.

owner_evidence: No CODEOWNERS found. Depth-one history is insufficient to infer ownership reliably.
